name: Mount Whitney Trail
disclaimer: Verify permits, water, and conditions with Inyo National Forest before you go. Afternoon thunderstorms and altitude are the real dangers. This is a companion, not a substitute for a map and judgment.

features.name: Whitney Portal
features.notes: Trailhead (~8,360′). Store, grill, water, restrooms, last food. A Whitney Zone permit is required and overnight trips need a bear canister. Fill up and start in the dark on summit day.

features.name: Lone Pine Lake
features.notes: First lake (~9,960′), a short spur off the main trail. Just below the Whitney Zone boundary — good water and a rest spot.

features.name: Outpost Camp
features.notes: Lower camp (~10,360′) in a meadow by Lone Pine Creek. More sheltered/treed than Trail Camp; water available. A milder acclimatization option.

features.name: Mirror Lake
features.notes: Lake at ~10,640′. Water; no camping. Steep switchbacks follow above here.

features.name: Trailside Meadow
features.notes: Small green meadow (~11,400′) with a seasonal creek. Often the last easy water before Trail Camp early/late season.

features.name: Trail Camp
features.notes: Highest camp (~12,000′) and the launch point for summit day. LAST reliable water before the 99 switchbacks — tank up and treat it. Exposed and cold; bear canister required, and marmots raid packs.

stay.unit: Whitney Zone overnight permit · treat & tank up on water here

features.name: Trail Crest
features.notes: Top of the 99 switchbacks (~13,600′) and the JMT/PCT junction. Many stash overnight gear here for the out-and-back to the summit. No water beyond this point.

features.name: Mt. Whitney Summit
features.notes: 14,505′ — highest point in the lower 48. Stone summit hut, sign the log. This is the HALFWAY point, not the finish: you still have ~11 mi and 6,000′ of descent back to Whitney Portal. Turn around early — be heading down before afternoon storms build, and pace water/energy for the way out.

global.name: Altitude (AMS)
global.notes: You'll sleep at ~12,000′ and summit at 14,505′. Headache/nausea/dizziness = AMS. Hydrate, go slow, and DESCEND if it worsens — altitude is the most common reason people turn around.

global.name: Afternoon thunderstorms
global.notes: Sierra storms build by midday in summer. Summit early and aim to be below Trail Crest by noon. Lightning on the exposed ridge is deadly — turn around if storms are building.

global.name: Permits & bear canister
global.notes: A Whitney Zone permit is required (overnight via lottery/reservation). Overnight trips must carry a bear canister. Pack out everything, including WAG bags — human waste must be carried out in the Whitney Zone.

global.name: Water strategy
global.notes: Reliable water: Lone Pine Lake, Outpost Camp, Mirror Lake, and Trail Camp. Treat everything. NO water above Trail Camp — carry enough for the summit push and back (3+ L on summit day).

global.name: The 99 switchbacks & cables
global.notes: The relentless switchbacks climb from Trail Camp (~12,000′) to Trail Crest (~13,600′). A cabled section can hold ice/snow early season — check conditions; an ice axe + microspikes may still be needed in mid-July after a big snow year.

global.name: Marmots & cold
global.notes: Marmots at Trail Camp chew through packs for salt — never leave gear unattended. Summit temps can be below freezing with wind even in July; carry warm layers, gloves, and a hat.

itinerary.sub: Hike Whitney Portal → Trail Camp (~6.0 mi, +3,700′) · acclimatize, tank up on water
Trail Camp → summit (~4.7 mi, +2,400′), then descend all the way to the Portal

blocks.th: ⚠️ Summit day — Trail Camp → summit → out
blocks.html: Alpine start in the dark, summit by mid-morning, then pack up and descend all the way to the Portal. The single biggest day of the trip. Be below Trail Crest before afternoon storms build.
Start at ~3 AM by headlamp so you summit with hours of weather margin.

sched.pl: Leave Trail Camp · headlamp up the 99 switchbacks
Trail Crest · stash overnight gear, carry a summit pack + water
Summit (14,505′) · photos, sign the log, then turn around
Descend to Whitney Portal · pace your knees on the long drop

blocks.html: Treat all water; last reliable source is Trail Camp — carry 3+ L for the summit push. Watch for AMS and descend if it worsens. Summit early and be off the exposed ridge before noon in monsoon season. Bear canister required; marmots raid unattended packs.
